I'm no expert on video, but I work with images professionally... And I'm going to say that it's not possible, in a "correct" way. Just like you can't convert an image to a higher resolution, you can't convert a video to a higher frame rate without sacrificing quality.

You can't create what's not there... Including pixels and frames. I remember artists using a technique, like you're describing, to simulate stop-motion animation. They'll film at a lower frame rate, and scale it up and play it at a higher frame rate... Or something to that nature. And it makes your animation appear as if it was stop-motion, like the old claymation videos/movies.

Essentially, you can downsample, but not correctly upsample.

It's quite possible to "create what's not there" using morphing, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphing

Fifth Gear did this to make slo-mo footage.

A lot of people are going to (correctly) say it's possible to generate missing frame data by interpolating the frames around them in some way. You're right in pointing out that these generated frames won't be great approximations of what the missing frames would actually have looked like, but I wanted to make sure that point was made really clearly.

Yes, you can regenerate missing data. No, it doesn't look right. A lot of the motion-sickness-inducing jelly-wobbling you see in youtube-stabilized videos is caused by this problem. Youtube is attempting to make it look like the camera was moving along a different path than it actually was, and trying to generate the "correct" image data after the fact really makes me want to hurl sometimes.

Where do you get this information?

youtube stabilization works by zooming in a bit so there is wiggle room on the sides, and then it moves the video around in opposing directions according the the shakiness, then cuts a new video from the common area within the zoom.

Frame interpolation works just fine. If you have a powerful enough CPU, then SVP on windows or a newer build of MPV on linux will do it perfectly fine. In between each native frame it calculates where each pixel would have been, and creates a new frame. We are talking about a single pixel or so of movement (per pixel), it's really not magic like so many people seem to think it is (nor is it impossible, nor does it negatively affect quality).

I got the information from memory of personal projects over a few years. I've actually done a lot of poking at vision-based robotics systems, so I have more-than-average experience with video processing algorithms, but it's all from the perspective of extracting useful information out of video streams, not making them look good. Even so, it's all amateur level stuff until I get my engineering degree finished.

Anyway, you made me doubt my recollection, so I did some quick searching and here's the paper where Google researchers describe the method they developed. It turns out that I did misspeak - the image data itself isn't "reconstructed" it's just cropped according to the "camera path" that is reconstructed (and it's not quite as simple as "moving around in opposing directions"). It still shits itself in nausea-inducing ways if the original footage isn't a nice wide shot with simple camera moves and a detailed background.

EDIT: It occurs to me that it might not be obvious why simple cropping and panning can fuck up perspective and such: A lot of people don't think about the fact that a camera lens induces a significant amount of distortion in the image that does things like bend straight lines and make distances between objects appear much closer or farther than they actually are. The exact effects depend strongly on the position of the area in question within the field of view of the lens, and also on the exact position of the camera with respect to the subject. By cropping the output image down, and moving the cropped area all around the captured image, the lens distortions change over time, which isn't really normal. By faking a camera movement that is smoother than the actual camera movement, the fast distortions of perspective caused by the camera's location in space don't match up with the smooth motions of the "fake camera."

You're right that most of the pixels that would be interpolated are very small, single-pixel differences, but that's not always the case, especially with particularly fast motion at low frame rates like 24fps. Then add in the problems involved with matching the kind of motion blur hollywood films have. It's just not a fun proposition.

And seriously, the math is just not on your side. It's just straight-up impossible to accurately recreate what the camera would have seen in a frame of video that wasn't ever actually recorded. You can make approximations that can look good in most cases, but if there was an odd scenario, the difference would be striking. Say, if a bright light just happened to be flickering at the same frequency as the camera shutter, interpolating between the captured frames would result in something that looks alright but leaves out the 50% of frames that are much brighter (or darker) than the captured video stream. Dumb example, sure, but it illustrates a problem that pops up all the time with fast camera motion or subject motion.

Ok, now we agree lol. With frame interpolation though, it's not trying to stabilize anything, and is interpolating professional quality video, not someones cellphone shit. If we look at a specific pixel, lets call it 1x1 (very top left pixel on screen/in the video), an interpolation algorithm looks at where 1x1 is in frame 1, and looks at it again in frame 2. Then it guesses where it will be (or what will be in its place) if there were a "1.5", and injects that between frame 1 and 2.

A race player can have multiple heroes, these heroes cannot ascend.

A Race starts with 30 Savagery. The Savagery they were created with will reflect the strength of their first stronghold.

A controlled Race gains 10 Savagery on the Sabbat.

Races can:

* Expand their strongholds & dominion (health) * Expand their economy & trade (Purchasing power for future use) * Develop Technology (Development power for future use) * Train armies in Combat * Train armies in Magic * Attack Races, Heroes & Demigods

Races battling other Races can earn modifiers based on:

* Combat Advantage: +1 Savagery * Magic Advantage: +1 Savagery * Technology Advantage: +1 Savagery * Location Advantage: +1 Savagery * Numbers Advantage: +1 Savagery These modifiers will be awarded courtesy of the Arbiters

Races cannot do God or Demigod things.

* If a Race loses all strongholds the race becomes extinct.

### 4.5 Permanents

* Armies * Strongholds * Weapons * Artefacts * Demigods * .....

Anything that is on the board hold their Creation Value and their Powerscaling.

Players can build on what has been created in future posts where they add to it. You can only further strengthen something you could create

Using a permanent in an action will have it's Creation Value as a modifier in your favor.

>Example: A Demigod of 6 Savagery is attacking another Demigod of 3 Savagery. This action counts as 7 vs 3 before other votes are cast.

------------------------ ## 5. The Savagery system

[Savagery Infographic](https://i.sli.mg/fmiavs.jpg)

### 5.1 Votes Each player regardless of what they play has 1 free unscaled vote on each action. You can cast this by writing Aye or Nay on top of your post. You only have 1 vote in each post. If you casted your vote on the original action you do not get a vote on the curse by another player.

You can also modify strengthen your vote by using your Savagery points. You will then lose these points.

[Here we have only Zille losing 3 Savagery](https://i.sli.mg/ZRQ4wV.png) After this action Zille will be at 27 Savagery, regardless of outcome.

Players can spend Savagery in the comments as well.

### 5.2 Modifiers Modifiers are a free addition to your voice. If a modifier applies you will receive it at the discretion of the mods. The modifier is mandatory.

Examples of modifiers

* Creation Value of a permanent * Domains * Combat Advantages * Plot Armour * ...

When gods have conflicting domains, the more specific domain wins the domain bonus.

>For Example: Awry, God of Mischief tries to steal something. His domain is relevant and so the action would start at 2 VS 0. However Valdi, God of Thieves dislikes the action and tries to prevent it. Awry will not get the +1 Domain bonus. That bonus will instead go to Valdi. The action would be at 1 VS 2

When races are evenly matched, certain advantage might not be awarded to either one.

### 5.3 The Dice

The roll always puts Low = Worst outcome for OP.

An action of 6 VS 3

Roll | Effect --- | --- 1 | Negative 2 | Negative 3 | Negative 4 | Positive 5 | Positive 6 | Positive 7 | Positive 8 | Positive 9 | Positive

### 5.4 Creation posts

Posts that create or modify a permanent will be rolled on as creation post

In the Example above, Zille creates Superglue and has 5 Savagery in favour and 2 Savagery against.

Zille's superglue is not an artefact, therefore future interactions will be scaled by 1 as any other mortal thing.

A roll table will be created.

Roll | Effect --- | --- 1 | Zille fails to create Superglue 2 | Zille creates Superglue of 0 Savagery turning it into a glue that doesn't hold anything together 3 | Superglue of 1 Savagery 4 | Superglue of 2 Savagery 5 | Superglue of 3 Savagery 6 | Superglue of 4 Savagery 7 | Superglue of 5 Savagery

!dice 1d7 - Result 6 => Zille creates a superglue of strength 4 Savagery.

Any God, Demigod, Hero, Race that becomes stuck in this superglue will need to pass an action where they overcome the strength of the glue.

### 5.5 Crossroad posts

Posts with a black and white result will be rolled on as crossroad posts.

Mar'dy, our hero1, becomes stuck in Supeglue1. Because the superglue has the same powerscaling, we see no multiplier. [He makes an action to break free.](https://i.sli.mg/Qndsy1.png) This action costs him 2 Savagery, regardless of outcome.

Roll | Effect --- | --- 1 | Mar'dy Fails to break free 2 | Mar'dy Fails to break free 3 | Mar'dy Fails to break free 4 | Mar'dy Fails to break free 5 | Mar'dy is out! 6 | Mar'dy is out! 7 | Mar'dy is out! 8 | Mar'dy is out! 9 | Mar'dy is out! 10 | Mar'dy is out!

!dice 1d10 - Result 5 => Mar'dy is out!

*If Mar'dy fails to break free, he will need a race, god, demigod or hero to come break him out as he cannot repeat this action.*

### 5.6 Conflict posts For damaging and offensive actions we use the Conflict system.

After all votes, modifiers, Curses/blessings and Savagery has been spent the arbiters will make up a roll table. The more Savagery is spent on a conflict, the harsher potential outcome may be for one of the evolved.

A Savagery: 7 | B Savagery: 4

Roll | Damage to A | Damage to B --- | --- | --- 1 | 4 | 0 2 | 3 |0 3 | 2 |0 4 | 1 |0 5 | 0 |1 6 | 0 |2 7 | 0 |3 8 | 0 |4 9 | 0 |5 10 | 0 |6 11 | 0 |7

2 Dice will be thrown, the first shows the damage to the offender. The second the damage to the defender.

Depending on the conflict, the results of this outcome will be translated into story in the Resolution text posted by the arbiters.

**Autodefend** - On conflict posts the arbiters will assume that the target automatically defends itself before resolution is made up.

### 5.7 Curses & Blessings

Gods can curse and bless anything in the comments. Curses & Blessings always happen at the powerscale of the original action.

Resolution of Curses & Blessings happens in the comments according to the "Creation system".

The final Savagery result of a curse is detracted from the OP. The final Savagery result of a blessing is added to the OP.

For the effects of the curse/blessing addendums will be made to original post in the Resolution text posted by the arbiters.

## Secrets

A secret action has a 5% chance of being discovered.

On a 1/d20 Arbiters will flair the post as Discovered, opening up interaction by all other players.

Otherwise the action is flaired as Secret. What happens in secret actions cannot be use by the other players to metagame against you. Other players cannot interfere with your secret action.

If you wish you can share a secret action with other players, the players part of a secret may interact.
